notes: Phase 3. The markup names no Bulma class for anything this product has an
opinion about — `bk-*` throughout — and the ledger is what makes that
checkable rather than aspirational.
Bulma is a class-based library, so unlike the shadcn study the verifier can
see the vocabulary directly. What it still cannot see is the page's one
COMPOSITION rule: the search panel's gold frame measures 1.75:1 against
white and 5.84:1 against the navy band, so it is only accessible in the
context it was designed for. No token can prevent someone dropping it onto
a white section. It is written into the pattern's `notes` and it is
advice, not a gate — saying so is the honest half.
EXTEND THE COMPONENT, NEVER A SHARED MODIFIER.
Bulma `is-primary`, `is-info` and `is-rounded` appear on several component
families, so `@extend` has to generate the cross product. The first version of
this product layer produced 84 selectors like `.bk-tab.bk-score`, and the score
badge inherited `.button` rules and lost its type size — a correctness bug, not
only bloat.
`@extend .button` and `@extend .card` are cheap and correct: they buy padding,
focus, disabled state and transitions. The modifier two or three colours come
from tokens instead, which is also more faithful — a brand hover is a chosen
value, not the base shifted by a fixed lightness delta.

button.intent: A control that performs an action. Two emphases: the gold CTA and the everyday white chip.

primary.intent: The one action a screen exists for. Gold, and used sparingly — Booking puts exactly one on a results row.
primary.diverges: Bulma colour MODIFIERS are shared across component families, so extending `is-primary` also pulls in `.tag.is-primary` and generates a cross product — measured at 84 nonsense selectors, and a score badge that inherited `.button` rules and lost its type size. This extends `.button` for the anatomy and names the two colours from tokens, which also buys a real brand hover (#e5a400) instead of Bulma computing one by shifting lightness a fixed delta.

secondary.intent: The everyday action, and the one Booking actually uses most: Register, Sign in, Show more, Check other dates.
secondary.diverges: White fill, blue ink, no border. Two declarations over Bulma `.button`, and the border width must be `0px` rather than `0`: Bulma computes padding as `calc(0.5em - var(--bulma-button-border-width))` and a unitless zero makes that calc invalid, collapsing the padding to nothing. The button rendered 21px tall instead of 35 and read as a text link.

tabs.intent: Which one of a set you are looking at. Booking uses it twice — the product nav in the header and the category filter carousel — and they are the same component.

list.diverges: Bulma `.tabs` is an underlined bar. Booking uses a wrapping row of pills, so this is three flex declarations rather than a fight with the library anatomy.

tab.intent: One entry. Idle is transparent; chosen takes a line in the interactive ink.
tab.diverges: Extends `.button` for the anatomy, then three corrections: pill radius from `radius-pill` rather than `@extend .is-rounded` (that modifier is shared with `.tag`, `.input` and `.select`), Booking taller 11px/16px padding through Bulma own padding variables, and `color: inherit` when idle.
tab.notes: ONE CLASS, TWO CONTEXTS, NO VARIANT. Chosen reads `fg-link` and the border reads `currentColor`, so on the page it is blue on white and inside `[data-surface="inverted"]` it is white on navy — the context supplies the ink. Booking ships an on-brand modifier for this; the context replaces it. `aria-current` drives the header instance and `aria-pressed` the filter row, so the accessible state and the visual state cannot drift apart.

search.intent: The destination/dates/occupancy panel. Booking's signature component and the reason anyone recognises the page.

default.diverges: Bulma's `field is-grouped` puts controls in a row; it does not frame them, and it certainly does not make the frame the loudest element on the page. Built from tokens instead. The frame is `bg-action` used as a BORDER — the same token doing a second job, legitimate because a 4px band is a non-text element where WCAG asks 3:1.
default.notes: COMPOSITION RULE, not enforceable: the gold frame reads 1.75:1 on white and 5.84:1 on the navy band. Place this panel on `data-surface="inverted"` only. The submit inside it is `selected` (blue) rather than `action` — a gold button inside a gold frame disappears.

score.intent: A review score. A stamp, not a label.

default.intent: The score badge beside a listing's review summary.
default.diverges: Bulma's `.tag` is a pill sized to its text. This is a fixed square with one corner squared off, so a column of them lines up whether the score is 8.0 or 10. Extending `.tag` would leave its padding and line-height fighting the fixed size, so it is built from tokens.
default.notes: Takes `bg-info`, which this theme points at the navy. That is the same navy as the header band — a real and slightly awkward fact about the brand rather than a shortcut.

listing.intent: One property in the results. The unit the whole product is built around.
listing.namespaceNote: `bk-price__was` and `bk-price__now` live in the listing's rail and are anatomy, not variants.

default.intent: The horizontal row: image, content, price rail.
default.diverges: Bulma's `.card` is a vertical stack. A results page is a scan down a column of prices, so this is a three-column grid with the rail right-aligned — the numbers form a column the eye can run down. Geometry only; every colour still comes from `.card` through the adapter.

badge.intent: A short status stamp on a listing.

deal.diverges: Square-cornered and bolder than Bulma's pill. Colour untouched: `is-success` already resolves to the brand green through the adapter.
deal.notes: A status colour reporting a fact about the price. It never marks an action — the button beside it is the action.
